text:
nina: Heads-up from recruiting  we have 3 new hires starting between Dec 20Dec 28. Our year-end accrual cutover normally prorates start-of-employment to the next period, but holiday blackout and payroll freeze complicate their initial PTO balances. Anybody seen a clean precedent?

marc: We've handled similar cases before: option A) grant full new-hire allotment pro-rated by days worked in the first pay period; option B) grant a fixed onboarding PTO bucket (e.g., 8 hours) that doesn't count against carryover. For hires starting during the shutdown window, we typically allow an exception so they can book emergency time.

fay: We should also think about managers approving onboarding PTO vs. formal accrual. If we auto-grant a small onboarding bucket, managers can approve days off without payroll changes. Keeps finance happy.

devin: Payroll note: any accrual changes need to be recorded before payroll cutoff (2026-01-01 00:00 UTC). For hires starting after cutoff, accruals kick in next pay period. For exceptions, HR needs to submit a manual payroll adjustment request.

nina: Proposed short rule for this cycle: 1) New hires starting within the blackout get a 1-day onboarding PTO credit (8h) automatically; 2) If they start earlier and work at least 3 days before cutoff we prorate full accrual; 3) Managers can request additional onboarding PTO via HR case for special circumstances.

marc: Sounds reasonable. Can we add an explicit line that onboarding PTO does not count toward year-end carryover? Prevents gaming.

fay: Yes. Also add guidance for part-time hires: onboarding credit should be pro-rated to FTE (e.g., 4h for 0.5 FTE).

devin: I'll file the payroll adjustment template and add the deadline. HR bot: create a policy blurb draft and a template spreadsheet for adjustments.

hr-bot: automated: Draft created at https://redwood.internal/hr/newhire-accrual-exception. Template: NewhirePayrollAdjustment.tsv.

nina: Awesome. Action items: 1) fay: add part-time pro-rate language and example calc (ETA 24h) 2) devin: upload payroll adjustment template to finance (ETA EOD) 3) marc: add non-carryover sentence to the PTO policy (ETA 48h). I'll send a short how-to to hiring managers once live.

marc: Quick example calc to include in the doc:
```
Daily accrual rate = annual_hours / 260
Onboarding credit (FTE 1.0) = 8h
Part-time onboarding = 8h * FTE
```

fay: I'll add that and an example for a 0.6 FTE.

nina: Thanks all. Closing when the policy blurb and template link are posted here. :white_check_mark:
